title: Closure of a product image for schemes over a field
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $A,B,X,Y$ schemes [def-pc-scheme] with specified morphisms to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $f:A\to X$ and $g:B\to Y$ commute with those structure morphisms. Let $j_X:C_f\hookrightarrow X$ and $j_Y:C_g\hookrightarrow Y$ be the reduced induced closed subschemes on the closed subsets $\overline{f(|A|)}$ and $\overline{g(|B|)}$, respectively [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. With fibre products and their induced morphisms as in [def-pc-fibre-product], the following equality of subsets of $|X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}Y|$ holds: $\overline{(f\times_k g)(|A\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}B|)}=(j_X\times_k j_Y)(|C_f\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}C_g|)$. All closures are Zariski topological closures. No quasi-compactness, finite-type, reducedness or separatedness assumption on $A,B,X,Y$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 04Q0 (lemma-closure-image-product-map), statement and proof; the product of closed subsets is expressed as the image of the product of their reduced induced closed subschemes.

proof.text: Put $P=X\times_kY$, write $p_X,p_Y$ for its projections, put $F=f(|A|)$, $G=g(|B|)$, and let $E=(f\times_kg)(|A\times_kB|)$. The image formula of [lem-sfb-scheme-pullback-point-images], applied over $\operatorname{Spec}k$, gives $E=p_X^{-1}(F)\cap p_Y^{-1}(G)$. Apply the same formula to $j_X,j_Y$. Since their images are $\overline F,\overline G$ by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], the image $H=(j_X\times_kj_Y)(|C_f\times_kC_g|)$ equals $p_X^{-1}(\overline F)\cap p_Y^{-1}(\overline G)$. Morphisms of schemes are continuous, so $H$ is closed and contains $E$. Thus $\overline E\subseteq H$.

source.place: Tag 04Q0, image identification; Tag 047B, first sentence of proof.

proof.text: Write $Q=C_f\times_kC_g$, $q=j_X\times_kj_Y$, and let $r_X,r_Y$ be the projections of $Q$. The closed immersions $j_X,j_Y$ are homeomorphisms onto their images [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Hence $F_0=j_X^{-1}(F)$ is dense in $|C_f|$: every nonempty relative open subset of $\overline F$ meets $F$, by the definition of closure. Likewise $G_0=j_Y^{-1}(G)$ is dense in $|C_g|$. To show $H\subseteq\overline E$, let $O\subseteq|P|$ be open with $O\cap H\ne\varnothing$. Then $W=q^{-1}(O)$ is nonempty open in $|Q|$, by continuity and $q(|Q|)=H$.

source.place: Tag 047B, replacement of the ambient schemes by the reduced image closures; relative-density and neighbourhood reformulation.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-scheme-over-field-universally-open] the projection $r_X:Q\to C_f$ is open (use $X=C_g$, $S=C_f$, and interchange the two fibre-product factors). Consequently $r_X(W)$ is nonempty open and meets the dense subset $F_0$. Choose $c\in r_X(W)\cap F_0$. Form the scheme-theoretic fibre $Q_c=Q\times_{C_f}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(c)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre], whose point space identifies with $r_X^{-1}(c)$. The inverse image $W_c$ of $W$ in $Q_c$ is therefore nonempty open. The fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $Q_c$ with $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(c)\times_k C_g$: both represent pairs consisting of a map to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(c)$ and a compatible map to $C_g$. Apply [lem-sc-scheme-over-field-universally-open] again, now with $X=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(c)$ and $S=C_g$. The projection of $W_c$ to $C_g$ is nonempty open, so meets $G_0$.

source.place: Tag 047B, nonempty open W, open first projection, and open projection of the residue-field fibre; openness input Tag 0383 (morphisms-lemma-scheme-over-field-universally-open).

proof.text: Choose $d\in G_0$ in that image and a point $t\in W_c$ projecting to $d$. Its image $w\in W$ satisfies $r_X(w)=c$ and $r_Y(w)=d$. Thus $p_X(q(w))=j_X(c)\in F$ and $p_Y(q(w))=j_Y(d)\in G$. By the image formula proved in step 1, $q(w)\in E$; since $w\in W$, also $q(w)\in O$. Every open subset meeting $H$ therefore meets $E$, which gives $H\subseteq\overline E$ by the neighbourhood definition of closure. Together with step 1 this is the asserted equality. If $H$ is empty, step 1 already gives $E=\varnothing$ and the equality, so no nonemptiness hypothesis has been introduced.

source.place: Tag 047B, final choice of b and nonempty intersection with W; Tag 04Q0, conclusion.

proof_origin.place: Tag 04Q0 (lemma-closure-image-product-map), expanded using Tag 047B (lemma-closure-of-product), with its Tag 0383 openness input.

lean.statement: theorem closure_range_pullback_map_over_field (k : Type u) [Field k] {A B X Y : Scheme.{u}} (a : A ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (b : B ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (x : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (y : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (f : A ⟶ X) (g : B ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≫ x = a) (hg : g ≫ y = b) : closure (Set.range (pullback.map a b x y f g (𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) ((Category.comp_id a).trans hf.symm) ((Category.comp_id b).trans hg.symm))) = Set.range (pullback.map ((vanishingIdeal (TopologicalSpace.Closeds.closure (Set.range f))).subschemeι ≫ x) ((vanishingIdeal (TopologicalSpace.Closeds.closure (Set.range g))).subschemeι ≫ y) x y (vanishingIdeal (TopologicalSpace.Closeds.closure (Set.range f))).subschemeι (vanishingIdeal (TopologicalSpace.Closeds.closure (Set.range g))).subschemeι (𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (Category.comp_id _) (Category.comp_id _))
